To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of beliefs observed in this study are consistent with previous studies on milk and dairy product consumption, and consumers’ concerns about origins are novel.

the consumption of milk and cheese among Canadian adults is influenced by a wide range of beliefs, including health effects, taste, socioaffective aspects, practicality and the influence of family and friends, health care professionals and advisors, media, and industry.

1) Health, taste, socio affective aspects, practicality and price were salient beliefs for milk and cheese; 2) Health professionals and family were the most influential sources; 3) Health status, price and taste are major barriers; 4) Men and low consumers are more influenced by industry, politics and animal and environmental concerns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the beliefs of Canadian adults regarding milk consumption?
the development of effective strategies to promote milk and cheese consumption in the Canadian adult populations.
the beliefs that people have about milk and cheese consumption, which are important determinants of their behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

milk and cheese consumption is affected by a variety of factors, which can be grouped into three categories (health and nutritional value, socio-affective and practical aspects) and which can be further divided into 12 themes.
the salient beliefs underlying milk and cheese consumption are consistent with earlier findings, with the addition of concerns about origins of the product.
the most important beliefs regarding milk consumption are: (1) the product is healthy, (2) it is good for the body, and (3) it is good to drink milk for the health of one’s bones, teeth, and muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most important beliefs regarding the consumption of milk and cheese are health effects, taste, socioaffective and practical aspects.
consumers have a variety of reasons for choosing or not choosing to consume dairy products, and the most important factors are related to health and taste.
consumers are concerned with the health and safety of the product, the taste and pleasure of the food, and the practical aspects of the product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the promotion of milk consumption should focus on health, taste, socio-emotional aspects, price, and availability of products.
consumers’ beliefs regarding milk and milk products are complex and multifaceted.
a variety of strategies are needed to address the barriers and facilitators to milk and cheese consumption among different groups.
